nodes.norm_label: chief section — the event waiter (action zero step 10)

nodes.label: Fleet manifest arming (--legs-from)
nodes.rationale: Keeping the leg set in a manifest the tick re-reads every sample removes the need to restart the waiter on every dispatch and wrap.

nodes.label: WAKE event types (telegram, tick, underfilled, tick-fail, succession, relay-on-live, holds)
nodes.norm_label: wake event types (telegram, tick, underfilled, tick-fail, succession, relay-on-live, holds)
nodes.rationale: Waking only when two consecutive samples differ from the last seen action key avoids noisy wakes while still surfacing leg, PR, dispatch and board changes.

nodes.label: Event waiter (replaces tick/telegram Monitor loops)
nodes.rationale: A Monitor arm is capped at 30 min and each expiry wasted a full-context turn, so loops are pure code and only a real event re-invokes the chief.

nodes.label: Waiter heartbeat file (<inbox>.wait)
nodes.rationale: Because tick.sh's own tick= field reads UNKNOWN and a SIGKILLed or low-memory-killed waiter is otherwise silent, the heartbeat is the liveness signal.

nodes.label: Permission rule for console-wait.sh launch
nodes.rationale: The allow rule is spelled relative with no leading glob because a glob could span quotes and let a bash -c wrapper match, and the harness refuses $VAR expansions before reading the allow list.

nodes.label: Script relay (R0) wrapping workers
nodes.rationale: Letting the waiter wrap WRAPPED/MERGED workers with bounded scripts absorbs routine bookkeeping without waking the chief, while the chief keeps every authority write.
